pricing_free_tier: not stated (open-source toolkit)
rate_limits: not stated on the pages we checked

name: Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
assets_covered: card payments (initial version); x402 stablecoin sample
live_vs_paper: specification, SDK and code samples (v0.2); not a hosted payment service
order_approval_safety: user intent and authorization travel as signed, tamper-evident mandates: a Checkout Mandate shared with the merchant and a Payment Mandate shared with the credential provider and networks; the open Payment Mandate captures constraints such as budget and allowed instruments for autonomous purchases, the closed stage authorizes a specific amount; human-present and human-not-present flows; the page doesn't say who enforces the constraints
pricing_free_tier: free open protocol (Apache-2.0)

name: LumiBot
assets_covered: stocks; ETFs; options; futures; forex; crypto; prediction markets
live_vs_paper: backtest, paper and live (self-hosted); the strategy class can stay the same, but startup code must call Strategy.backtest() for history or run_live()/Trader.run_all() for a broker. Alpaca paper is PAPER true or ALPACA_IS_PAPER, and the CLI has lumibot run --paper. Alpaca, Tradier, Interactive Brokers and Tradovate document paper or demo accounts; CCXT can use sandbox true where the exchange has a testnet. Setting IS_BACKTESTING=false does not by itself turn a backtest-only file into broker trading.
order_approval_safety: open-source (GPL-3.0) Python framework. AI strategies can set research agents to allow_trading=False and let one agent with allow_trading=True submit orders through the same order pipeline as a Python strategy. No per-order human confirmation is documented in the library. Named brokers: Alpaca, Interactive Brokers, Tradier, Charles Schwab, Tradovate, TopstepX via ProjectX, Bitunix and Polymarket, plus crypto exchanges through CCXT (the broker page says nine direct integrations, and the installed CCXT version lists 100+ exchange ids; the agent docs say LumiBot does not claim every CCXT exchange). 2,164 GitHub stars on Oct 24, 2026. Free skills for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor: https://github.com/Lumiwealth/lumibot-trading-skills (MIT).
pricing_free_tier: free, open source (GPL-3.0). You pay broker commissions, any market-data plan, and AI model calls if you use agents.

name: Vibe-Trading
assets_covered: stocks (US, HK, China A-shares, UK, Canada, India, Korea, Brazil and more); crypto; futures; forex
live_vs_paper: backtest, paper and live (self-hosted). v0.1.17 (Oct 21, 2026) adds daily paper trading with saved accounts that fill against completed daily bars and never reach a broker. Most of its 19 broker connectors also place orders on the broker's own paper account; bounded live orders are wired for Alpaca, Binance, OKX, Futu, Tiger, eToro, MetaTrader 5 and Robinhood (Robinhood is live-only). Paper vs live is a per-broker runtime check (account id, host, demo flag), not a setting the agent can flip, and brokers without such a signal are capped at paper and read-only.
order_approval_safety: open-source (MIT) Python trading agent from the Data Intelligence Lab at HKU (GitHub org HKUDS), with CLI, Web UI and an MCP server. Live orders need a mandate you commit (symbols, order size, exposure, leverage, daily cap) and run inside it with no per-order human confirmation; there is a kill switch (/halt) that cancels and flattens, mandate auto-expiry and an append-only audit ledger. IBKR, Scalable Capital, Trading 212 and Toss Securities connectors are read-only. It holds no funds: the broker holds the money and executes. 36,701 GitHub stars on Oct 26, 2026. The maker warns that the X account VibeTrading_HKU and any Vibe-Trading token or memecoin are not official; it has never launched a token.
pricing_free_tier: free, open source (MIT); pip install vibe-trading-ai. You pay your LLM provider plus any broker or data costs.
rate_limits: n/a (set by your LLM, data and broker providers)

name: SiftingIO MCP
assets_covered: US stocks; forex; crypto; commodities; DEX and on-chain data; SEC fundamentals
order_approval_safety: read-only market data: the hosted connector (10 read-only tools, OAuth sign-in to your SiftingIO account, used from ChatGPT or Claude) can't place orders or change your account; the open-source local server (siftingio-mcp on npm, MIT, 36 tools) reads your API key from the SIFTING_API_KEY environment variable
pricing_free_tier: free plan: 10,000 REST calls/month, no card (internal, non-commercial use); paid plans per market, e.g. Crypto Builder $79/mo and Pro $239/mo billed annually, US Stocks from $103/mo
rate_limits: free 60 requests/min; Builder 100/sec, Pro 150/sec, Ultra 250/sec; MCP calls use your plan's normal quota

name: CryptoQuant MCP Server
assets_covered: Bitcoin; Ethereum; XRP; TRON; stablecoins; ERC-20 tokens; alts
order_approval_safety: read-only on-chain and market data plus CryptoQuant research (9 tools); remote server at mcp.cryptoquant.com/mcp with OAuth 2.0 + PKCE sign-in using your API key or keyless on a shared pool; no trading or wallet access
pricing_free_tier: same plans and credits as the CryptoQuant API: Basic (free) 10,000 credits/month, 30 days of history, no on-chain data; on-chain data needs Professional or Premium; research and Quicktake tools free during the beta

name: CrowdWisdomTrading Setups API

pricing_free_tier: Setups API $299/month (separate from the trader product, which has a free tier); licensed for in-house use only, showing data to your clients needs a partner licence

name: Poly Research & Robotics
assets_covered: prediction markets (Polymarket): crypto, sports, esports and weather markets
order_approval_safety: free community and research for Polymarket bot builders: bot-building guides written for AI coding agents, trader reports, a strategy database and a Discord AI assistant; sells historical order-book, price-feed and TWAP datasets (Parquet, 30s to 1d); no trading access

name: CoinBoss API
assets_covered: crypto derivatives: liquidations, open interest, funding rates, long/short ratios, options; Hyperliquid positions and vaults; ETF flows, stablecoins, exchange balances
order_approval_safety: read-only public REST API at api.coinboss.com (65 documented endpoints); no trading, account or wallet access; works without a key, and an optional API key from the account center is for usage tracking
pricing_free_tier: free for now: all endpoints are free for everyone; paid tiers are announced as coming soon

name: Reslyce Flow MCP
assets_covered: US stock and ETF options flow (captured 0-2 DTE activity for 100 tracked tickers); large options prints ($1M+) out to 45 DTE; daily open interest by strike
order_approval_safety: read-only options-flow data: a hosted MCP server (https://www.reslyce.com/mcp) that ChatGPT, Claude and other MCP clients connect to with OAuth sign-in to your Reslyce account; it does not connect to a broker or place orders; covers only captured sessions and recorded contracts available to your account, not a complete options tape; index options such as SPX are not included
pricing_free_tier: needs Reslyce Flow access: 21 days free with no card, then $29/month if you continue; MCP and API access are included in the subscription
rate_limits: not stated on the pages we checked; data is live during the regular options session (9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. ET) and past sessions stay available for 60 days

name: DeskBot for Kalshi
assets_covered: Kalshi 15-minute up/down markets: 9 crypto (BTC, ETH, XRP, SOL, DOGE, HYPE, ZEC, NEAR, BNB), 5 metals, oil, natural gas and 3 currency pairs; Kalshi multi-leg combos and parlays; Polymarket 15-minute crypto Up/Down markets (on your own Polymarket account)
live_vs_paper: live on your own Kalshi account (and optionally Polymarket); starts in paper mode with simulated trading until you arm each market
order_approval_safety: closed-source desktop app for Mac and Windows that runs on your computer with your own Kalshi API key and trades 15-minute contracts automatically once a market is switched to live, with no per-trade approval; controls are a master switch, a live switch per market, stake, daily budget and open-position caps, and a daily loss limit that pauses new live entries ($15 by default); the main lane buys favorites priced around 90-95¢, so one loss can cost as much as a dozen or more wins; a copy mode mirrors a lead account's fills into other accounts; DeskBot never holds your money (funds stay in your Kalshi account); its 'Official coin' page says no DeskBot coin has launched yet and that a copycat 'Desk Bot Kalshi' coin is fake
pricing_free_tier: $19.99/month, first month $1; card required, renews monthly, no refunds once access is delivered; needs a funded Kalshi account (Kalshi trading fees apply)
rate_limits: n/a (Kalshi API limits apply); your computer must stay on while it runs

name: Craic Hub Exchange
assets_covered: Solana tokens (any token with a liquidity pool, including new pump.fun coins), routed through Jupiter; cross-chain swaps (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Arbitrum and more) through LI.FI; token launches on 8 chains
live_vs_paper: live only: real tokens on Solana and other mainnets; no paper or demo mode on the site
order_approval_safety: closed-source web swap site, token launchpad and Auto Trade (limit buys, take-profit and DCA as Jupiter on-chain orders); every trade, order and launch is signed in your own wallet and the site never asks for or stores seed phrases or private keys; once you sign a limit or DCA order, Jupiter fills it later without asking again; before Auto Trade opens your wallet the site decodes the transaction and blocks unknown programs, unlimited approvals and authority changes; no stop-loss orders (a stop-loss is only an alert with a one-tap sell link); the Craic Bot, a Telegram bot that turns plain-English requests into orders you sign, is marked coming soon and not open to the public; the site has its own memecoin, $CRAIC (a pump.fun token), that gives fee discounts, fees paid in it are burned, and burns, staking and holder rewards are stated as aims, not promises; the security page is the team's own self-review, not an independent audit; the site lists brand-new memecoins, which it calls very high risk
pricing_free_tier: no sign-up; swaps pay network and Jupiter fees plus a 0% to 0.75% platform fee (lower for $CRAIC holders); 25% off launch and featured-listing fees when paid in $CRAIC; Craic Bot plans listed at $15, $30 and $50/month (20% off in $CRAIC), payments not open yet
